section_summary: The section concludes an annex setting proposed assured production capacities for Japanese steel, iron, light metals, thermal power, and chemicals. It then contains memoranda transmitting occupation policy papers and two copies of SWNCC 302 on reducing Japanese industrial war potential. The report proposes destroying specialized war equipment, making excess industrial capacity available for reparations, and retaining enough capacity to support a civilian living standard based on 1930–1934.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 236/19, Annex to Appendix C: Assured Production Capacity Levels for Japan
subfiles.about: Calculates assured capacities for steel, pig iron, light metals, thermal electricity, caustic soda, soda ash, and chlorine.
subfiles.summary: The annex distinguishes capacity assured against final removal from additional capacity usable during the interim occupation period. It proposes assured levels of 2 million metric tons of steel ingot, 500,000 metric tons of pig iron, and 1 million kilowatts of public utility thermal generation. It also evaluates light metals and sets proposed assured capacities for caustic soda, soda ash, and chlorine using earlier consumption and population growth.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Transmits the approved SWNCC 236/19 capacity paper and requests presentation of Appendix C to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SWNCC 236/19, as amended, and requests a Far Eastern Commission policy decision on Appendix C.

subfiles.title: Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential: Memorandum for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports approval of SWNCC 302 and requests capacity studies and transmission of its conclusions to the U.S. Far Eastern Commission member.
subfiles.summary: Requests State Department studies and transmission of approved SWNCC 302 conclusions, with supporting material, to the U.S. member.

subfiles.title: Decision Amending SWNCC 302, Copy No. 55
subfiles.about: Announces approval of SWNCC 302 as amended and directs holders to replace two pages.
subfiles.summary: Announces approval and directs holders to substitute revised pages 7 and 9.

subfiles.title: Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential, SWNCC 302, Copy No. 55
subfiles.from: State-War-Navy Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East
subfiles.about: Recommends occupation measures for dismantling Japanese war industries and removing excess capacity through reparations.
subfiles.summary: The report calls for destruction of machinery dedicated to combat production and reparations claims on other equipment in primary war facilities and excess capacity in secondary and war-supporting industries. It uses average Japanese civilian consumption in 1930–1934 as the guide to peaceful industrial needs, while allowing for population growth, exports, and rebuilding. It assigns plant selection to SCAP, proposes occupation-period capacity ceilings, and reserves decisions on unclaimed assets and longer-term controls for later consideration.

subfiles.title: Decision Amending SWNCC 302, Copy No. 56
subfiles.about: A second copy announces approval of SWNCC 302 as amended and directs replacement of two pages.
subfiles.summary: Second copy of the approval notice directing substitution of revised pages 7 and 9.

subfiles.title: Reduction of Japanese Industrial War Potential, SWNCC 302, Copy No. 56
subfiles.from: State-War-Navy Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East
subfiles.about: A second copy presents proposed destruction, reparations, and capacity restrictions for Japanese industry.
subfiles.summary: This second copy repeats the recommendations to destroy specialized combat-production equipment and make other war-related or excess industrial capacity available for reparations. Its discussion explains the distinction between primary, secondary, and war-supporting industries and proposes the 1930–1934 civilian living standard as a basis for capacity estimates. The copy continues beyond page 256.
